structured_output.summary: Under the law in force for 2026, this household gets about $1,188 in refundable NY credits. The first part is the Empire State Child Credit of $307: $1,000 for a child aged three or younger, less 42 × $16.50 for federal AGI above $75,000. The second part is the new refundable NY child and dependent care credit of about $881 under Tax Law § 606(c-2), added by L.2026 ch.59 Part A and signed 2026-05-28: $3,000 of expenses × (55% − 0.00025 points per dollar of NY AGI above $15,000) ≈ 29.35%. The engine's ESCC is correct. For child care, though, it applied the old § 606(c) credit (60% of the federal credit, $360), which by its own terms now covers only tax years beginning before 2026. So the $667 reference rests on a repealed rule.
structured_output.engine_step_at_issue: New York's child and dependent care credit is $360: 60% of the federal credit (20% of $3,000). This is the pre-2026 § 606(c)(1) computation, which L.2026 ch.59 limited to tax years beginning before 2026-01-01 and replaced with the § 606(c-2) credit on qualifying expenses.
